title: BackOffice Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit BackOffice registration, discovery, content, security, and direct-module interaction.
owner: gExp/backoffice backend contracts and separate Axis frontend repository
summary: BackOffice owns registry/control-plane contracts and CMS seed content; Axis owns responsive renderers; business modules own APIs, data, validation, authorization, and execution.

sections.heading: Repository and runtime boundaries
items: Nodics is backend and API authority; nodicsaxis is a separate responsive React web client; each customer project deploys its own Axis instance.
Axis contains renderers, interaction, accessibility, session presentation, and generated clients but no business persistence, provider credentials, module startup, or authorization decisions.
Backend page and component content supplies labels, help, localization, and layout definitions while stable renderer keys map to small dedicated frontend files.

sections.heading: Registry and direct modules
items: Modules register asynchronously with BackOffice after startup using service identity, logical endpoints, capabilities, contract version, lease, and safe instance metadata.

Persistent logical registration survives restarts while expiring presence represents current instances. Registration outage is optional control-plane degradation and retries without request-path latency.
Axis discovers authorized modules through BackOffice, then calls Profile, CMS, Cron, Inventory, Pricing, Assistant, and other owning modules directly.

sections.heading: Content, workbench, and assistant
items: axisContentCatalog supplies login, recovery, lock, dashboard, navigation, workbench, documentation, and assistant presentation content and is imported idempotently as governed data.
Schema Workbench discovers authorized models, searches friendly code and description, invokes CRUD routes, and supports select-existing or nested creation across module relationships.
Axis Assistant streams conversations over authenticated SSE, retrieves governed evidence, proposes approved tools, obtains confirmation, and leaves target and Workflow authority intact.

sections.heading: Operations and acceptance
items: Test secure login and refresh, lock and logout, registry recovery, CMS fallback, direct-module denial, session context, navigation, responsive mobile webview, accessibility, and localization.
Test writable and read-only schemas, nested relations, tenant isolation, assistant reconnect and cancellation, contract drift, monoServer, distributed modules, outage, recovery, and load.
Document customer setup in nodicsaxis while full business/user capability guidance remains with Nodics backend documentation and authoritative content.

sections.heading: Architecture
items: Modules register asynchronously at startup with logical endpoint, capabilities, contract version, lease, and safe instance metadata.
Registry is persistent logical state plus expiring runtime presence, not a load balancer or data proxy.
Axis discovers authorized modules, then calls CMS, Profile, CronJob, NEMS, DEAP, Assistant, and other modules directly.
CMS content defines pages/components/labels; Axis maps stable renderer keys one component per renderer file.
Frontend contains no business rules, database access, or backend runtime.

sections.heading: Security and tests
items: Employee-only browser session, exact CORS/CSRF, HttpOnly refresh, in-memory access token, target authorization, module/service credential separation.

Registration retry/recovery, stale lease, duplicate instance, mono/distributed topology, CMS fallback, contract drift, direct-module outage, responsive/webview, accessibility, positive, negative, boundary, integration, and regression tests.
